gap: The deployed checkpoint restore case supplies a valid image. Local library corruption tests do not prove that the deployed replacement rejects a damaged image and fetches a healthy peer checkpoint.
scope: Harness only. No production runtime, hot path, format, service endpoint or deployment configuration changes. The case temporarily scales only pinned executor-0 to zero, then restores the complete saved job definition. Other groups keep running.
protocol: Wait for checkpoints on victim and peer; capture victim process identity and exact registered job.
Scale the pinned victim group to zero; require terminal allocations and no victim process before touching its files.
Copy the stopped victim checkpoint into a temporary directory; production restore must verify its manifest, image and declared block within120s. Temporary copies are removed on completion.
Fence the fault by the original image and manifest SHA256 values. Flip one image byte, preserve the manifest, remove other local bases and state. Keep the checkpoint block log.

Restore the exact job on success or failure. Within120s require a new process to report this image as CORRUPT, quarantine it, fetch a peer checkpoint and restore, in that order. Genesis fallback does not pass.

Verify the quarantined image and manifest against the fault hashes; verify the same replacement process still runs. Require executor progress/convergence and common receipt, validator and persisted-state checks.
workload: Uses the existing15-minute upper load window of archive corruption; stops unused load after recovery. No existing recovery deadline, offered rate or shard matrix changes. The harness adds bounded checkpoint copy/hash I/O and removes local temporary copies.

controls: Actual checkpoint bytes restore before fault, fail production verification after fault, then restore from an unmodified peer copy; quarantine hashes remain exact.
No quarantine, changed manifest, unchanged/old process, unrelated image rejection, wrong event order and genesis fallback do not certify recovery.
A stale baseline digest refuses injection before changing checkpoint or live state.
Only the selected pinned executor group changes; saved job and healthy peers retain their configuration.
The image selector chooses numeric newest, removes older local bases and retains the block log.

excluded_attempts: The first local fixture used block0, which BlockRange::ANY intentionally excludes. It is corrected to a real committed block1.
The writer snapshot channel first returns its genesis snapshot; the fixture now waits for committed block1.

remaining_gaps: ENOSPC and injected I/O failures remain open; this case covers corruption of the local recovery source and verified peer recovery only.
